title: C Quiz
description: Review the ideas from the lessons. Take your time. After each answer, read the note that explains the rule. You can try again.

questions.question: Which tool turns C source code into a program your computer can run?
questions.explanation: A compiler translates C source code into machine code. You then run the program it made.

questions.question: Fill the gap: gcc hello.c ___ hello names the output program hello.
questions.explanation: The -o flag chooses the output file name. On Windows, hello.exe is a useful name.

questions.question: Why does this statement fail to compile?
questions.explanation: Most C statements end with a semicolon. Write int pencils = 4; to finish this statement.
options: It needs a semicolon at the end

questions.question: What does this C program print?
questions.explanation: Both values are whole numbers, so integer division drops the fractional part.

questions.question: The C language promises that int is exactly four bytes on every computer.
questions.explanation: C sets minimum ranges, but sizes can differ. Use sizeof to ask for the size on your computer.

questions.question: Which numbers are printed?
questions.explanation: The loop starts at 0. It stops when i reaches 3 because i < 3 is then false.

questions.question: What should appear before a call to a function defined later in the file?
questions.explanation: A declaration tells the compiler how the function is called. For example: int add(int a, int b);
options: A declaration with its return type and inputs

questions.question: Which positions are valid in an array with three items?
questions.explanation: Array positions start at zero. The last valid position is one less than the item count.

questions.question: What numbers are printed?
questions.explanation: strlen counts the three letters. The array also stores a zero byte that marks the end of the string.

questions.question: Fill the gap: int* place = ___score; stores the address of score.
questions.explanation: The & operator gets the address of a variable. A pointer stores that address.

questions.question: If p points to a struct, p___score reads its score field.
questions.explanation: The arrow operator reaches a field through a pointer. With an ordinary struct variable, use a dot.

questions.question: An include guard starts with #ifndef and #define, then ends with ___.
questions.explanation: The guard lets a header body appear once even when several files include it.

questions.question: Which action is safe for int numbers[3] = {4, 5, 6};?
questions.explanation: Position 2 is inside this array. Positions 3 and -1 are outside it and must not be read.
